text:
liz: Quick sync — we need to finalize burst fairness tiers for Dedicated GA. Proposal draft below. Need launch criteria and pilot asks.

sam: High level looks good. Can we avoid naming tied to legal (eg. "tier 2"). Suggest names: baseline / elastic / priority.

kevin: Sales feedback: customers (Acme, FinCo) want predictable carryover. They'll only sign if we guarantee effective burst availability during key windows.

anya: From onboarding POV we need per-tenant dashboards and a clear degradation doc describing what customers see when burst is preempted.

miguel: Tech constraints: long burst windows (30m+) increase KV cache churn and scheduling complexity. We should cap carryover and enforce via token-bucket admission in the router.

asha: SLOs needed before launch. Propose: p95 latency target for burst paths and a burst error budget (eg. 0.5% monthly). Also need alert thresholds.

liz: Proposed fairness config (short):
- baseline: no burst (committed only)
- elastic: small burst (up to 5% of pool capacity, 5m window)
- priority: elevated burst (up to 20% sustained for 30m, limited carryover)
- enterprise: negotiated custom headroom
Need to confirm enforcement (tokens vs qps), billing model, and contract language.

sam: I prefer token-bucket per-tenant. Example pseudocode:```// refill per minute
bucket.capacity = commit_tokens * factor
on_request(tokens){ if bucket.take(tokens) allow else reject || fallback }
```This gives predictable billing and accounting.

miguel: Implementation note: admission control in routing + graceful fallback to lower-priority variants (smaller model or hosted) when tenant exceeds burst. Also limit carryover to 8 hours and hard cap at 3x commit to bound resource exposure.

kevin: Pricing ask: should burst be an add-on or baked into committed tiers? Sales wants a simple SKU: commit + optional burst add-on (monthly).

anya: Onboarding checklist: SDK flags for burst opt-in, preflight runbook, tenant dashboard, sample contract clause, and a two-week pilot playbook.

asha: Observability owners: I'll build dashboards (per-tenant burst usage, refill rate, p95/p99 latency) and alerts. Need metric names and tagging convention from eng.

liz: Launch checklist (GA gates):
- docs + engineering README
- pilot with 2 customers (Acme, FinCo) completed
- load test at 80% projected active burst load without violating core SLOs
- contract language reviewed by legal (soft vs hard SLA)

kevin: Legal wants "soft language" for burst but Sales still needs a commercial concession for enterprise pilots. We can offer a pilot SLA in appendices.

sam: Engineering sprint asks: 1) router token-bucket, 2) carryover/cap enforcement, 3) fallback path + metrics tags. Estimate: 3-4 sprints with one eng + one infra + one runtime.

miguel: FYI I pushed an early branch implementing token-bucket math and admission hooks. Will open PR today.

deploy-bot: deploy:feature/dedicated-burst-config merged to staging by miguel. CI passed :white_check_mark:

asha: Good. I'll start dashboard skeleton and alert rules. Will share JSON export for review by Friday.

kevin: :thumbsup: Sales can commit the Acme + FinCo pilots if engineering provides onboarding docs and a three-week onboarding window.

liz: Ok owners + dates:
- miguel/sam: prototype router token-bucket + PR by end of Sprint (owner: miguel)
- asha: dashboard + alerts by Friday (owner: asha)
- anya: pilot playbook + onboarding checklist by Wed (owner: anya)
- kevin: confirm pilot contracts + pilot dates with customers (owner: kevin)
- liz: write launch criteria doc and coordinate legal (owner: liz)

liz: Please react with priority (1 = must do for GA, 2 = nice-to-have) next 24h so we can scope sprint.

sam: 1 for router token-bucket, 1 for fallback path, 2 for carryover >8h.

miguel: 1 for admission control + fallback, 2 for carryover extension.

kevin: 1 for pilot playbook, 2 for public docs.

anya: 1 for onboarding checklist, 2 for post-launch runbook drills.

asha: 1 for dashboards and alerts, 2 for longer-term cost analytics.

liz: Thanks all — I'll synthesize votes and post a scoped plan tomorrow.
